opportunities.title: The 0-Day Found Itself: China's AI Agents Just Auto-Pwned a University Server
opportunities.why_now: Three outlets (Register, SecurityWeek, Hacker News) are independently confirming the first documented case of AI agents autonomously discovering and exploiting a zero-day, a watershed moment for the inevitable-breach thesis.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/analysis piece connecting the university hack to the parallel Amazon medical-imaging zero-day story — same actor class, two targets, one week

opportunities.title: Chase, Visa, Mastercard All Breached in One Week — Here's What Actually Got Stolen (and What Didn't)
opportunities.why_now: Three of the biggest names in finance just confirmed third-party breaches within days of each other, but researchers say the stolen data is phishing fuel, not account-drainer material — a nuance worth correcting before the panic headlines spread.
opportunities.angle: Myth-busting digest: separate the breach disclosure from the actual risk, with a practical 'what to watch for in your inbox' checklist

opportunities.title: SonicWall Just Told Gen 6 Firewall Customers: You're On Your Own, Even for Critical CVEs
opportunities.why_now: SonicWall's EOL-no-patch announcement for Gen 6 firewalls is a textbook patch-cadence failure story that leaves a huge installed base of perimeter devices permanently exposed.
opportunities.angle: Patch-cadence outrage post: name the affected models, explain the exposure window, and push readers toward an immediate migration checklist

opportunities.title: Armory Castle: Inside China's Siege on VMware vCenter — and Why Your Hypervisor Is the New Perimeter
opportunities.why_now: Dark Reading's naming of the 'Armory Castle' campaign against vCenter, paired with The Hacker News confirming active exploitation of VMware/Cisco/Apache flaws, signals a coordinated espionage push against virtualization infrastructure right now.
opportunities.angle: Threat-actor profile + patch-urgency sidebar listing every actively exploited CVE in the cluster

opportunities.title: The FBI's Own Crime Database May Have Just Been Hacked — Yes, That One
opportunities.why_now: A breaking, single-sourced AP report that the bureau's key national criminal justice database may be compromised is the kind of institution-trust-shaking story that demands immediate coverage before details firm up.
opportunities.angle: Fast-turn breaking-news post flagging what's confirmed vs. rumored, with a promise to update as facts emerge
